steps.message:
Before I write anything: this is an irreversible data deletion, so I want your explicit go-ahead first.

`users.notes` is a populated `TEXT` column and the README says production has 48,000 rows in `users`. `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` destroys whatever is in it for every one of those rows, and the migration is applied automatically by the deploy job. There's no rollback — the only recovery path would be a database restore. "We stopped using it" tells me the application no longer reads it, which isn't the same as the stored values being worthless.

One related detail: `schema.sql` is kept in sync by hand, so it needs the `notes` line removed alongside the migration.

steps.message:
Done, per your confirmation.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the hand-maintained mirror matches.

Verified by applying all three migrations in order to a scratch SQLite database; the resulting `users` schema is `id`, `email`, `created_at`.

One deployment note: `DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35+ (2021-03). Worth confirming the production engine is at least that before the deploy job runs, or the migration will fail with a syntax error rather than dropping anything.
